compare_blocks.title: The key difference

compare_blocks.body:
The premise is aligned conditions: the same monthly inspection, the same eleven findings, the same shutdown window and review deadline, the same approval authority. If one owns the review and the other only handles the shift, or one holds shutdown approval and the other does not, role will cover both columns.

Each row states the basis each may attend to and notes which axis it illustrates. Both types can use both approaches; the table describes only which is taken first more often, and is not a typing rule.

| The same scene (one inspection, the same eleven items, the same authority and deadline) | ESTP: the basis more likely attended to | ISFJ: the basis more likely attended to | What this row illustrates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Both organise follow-up for the same findings after applying mandatory safety controls | Apply the same follow-up criteria to the remaining findings | Weigh how each follow-up option affects the people relying on the area | Basis for judgement, leaning T/F |

compare_blocks.title: One-minute comparison

compare_blocks.body:
Two people in the same workshop rarely talk in generalities: one watches where an accident could happen, the other remembers who promised what. Part of that resemblance comes from the shared S — both talk in specific locations, specific people and specific dates, and neither stays at the level of slogans. But S only says sourcing prefers facts and experience; it does not say who is more careful, and does not say who is more practical.

The difference sits on three preferences. ESTP more often takes the facts on the floor in front of them (S), with attention and energy turned outward (E); ISFJ more often takes past experience and agreements already confirmed (S), with attention and energy turned inward (I). In judging, ESTP more often relies on criteria that can be applied consistently (T), and ISFJ more often counts people and values in (F). In outer work, ISFJ more often forms an arrangement and a conclusion (J), and ESTP more often keeps options (P).

The three are read separately. They do not combine into a scale of "who is more dependable", and cannot be replaced by "which step came first": registering before handling, and handling before registering, both occur in either person.

### Eleven findings: what each more often sorts by

With eleven items on the table, either may sort by urgency and either by closure. Which kind of basis is cited more often is a description of preference; the actual sequence is also constrained by risk level, qualifications and approval, shift duty, spare-part arrival and shutdown windows.

In this fictional inspection, immediate hazards and recurring problems both need attention. The site procedure determines what needs immediate action, regardless of who notices it.

Once required safety controls are in place, both can check which follow-up actions need an owner, a maintenance window or verification that the issue was resolved.

The two bases are usually mixed on one sheet: contain what has to be isolated immediately, then, with risk controlled, register owners, deadlines and review dates. That combination has nothing to do with type; it is ordinary safety management.

A fictional monthly inspection shows where the difference lies. After eleven findings, one colleague makes sure the findings reach the authorised team. The other confirms which follow-up actions have an owner and a review date, and flags three findings that also appeared last year. Either person could do both. At the month-end review, what tends not to be closed is not the most dangerous items but the ones needing a shutdown window — which has nothing to do with sorting preference and everything to do with maintenance windows, spare parts and approval progress.

Three things evidence the quality of rectification: whether the review record carries a signature, whether the same hazard recurs, and whether window-dependent items were scheduled into the maintenance plan. Those three check rectification quality only and cannot be turned around to infer a type; nor does the speed of the walk or the number of notices issued count.

Keep the counterexamples: asked for a closure rate, someone leaning to the ESTP side may build the sheet themselves and chase review dates; seeing pallets blocking a fire route, someone leaning to the ISFJ side may call people to clear it first and register afterwards. Role, duty, experience and deadline all rewrite the approach.

### Why Ti and Fe are shared but swapped

In the common four-function notation used here, ESTP is Se–Ti–Fe–Ni and ISFJ is Si–Fe–Ti–Ne. The shared Ti and Fe swap: ESTP has Ti second and Fe third, ISFJ has Fe second and Ti third.

The perceiving side changes entirely, direction included: ESTP uses Se to catch the scene and keeps Ni last; ISFJ draws on Si for past experience and keeps Ne last. A function position is an emphasis in the model, not the first and second step of an action, and it does not show who unpicks the causal chain first or who attends to people first.

Whether the third process (Fe for ESTP, Ti for ISFJ) carries an attitude label is not consistent across tables: some give an explicit attitude, some only the function name. This page takes the common version and states the arrangement; the disagreement does not change the first two positions and does not explain why a particular inspection did one item first. Both base descriptions are the [ESTP profile](/en/personality/estp) and the [ISFJ profile](/en/personality/isfj).
compare_blocks.title: Why they are easily confused

compare_blocks.body:
Scope note: what follows is a fictional inspection and a household-maintenance scene, covering communication, the organisation of information and negotiation over the division of work only, not handling procedure, qualification judgement or medical first aid. For a smell of gas or an injury, leave the hazardous area first, call for help, and act on local emergency and professional guidance; the type discussion does not enter those judgements.

Working together, the two easily get stuck when one has already started work and the other is still checking the sheet. That is rarely about who is right, but about which kind of information each handles first — or simply about who was closer to the scene.

### After the inspection, who watches the shutdown window

(Fictional scene.) The division follows authority, experience and shift duty, not type. Handling and tracking are complementary tasks: the person on the floor knows what can be controlled on the spot and what it needs; the review owner knows the window, the spare parts and the approval progress. A workable move is for both to design one three-cell card — today, this week, needs a window — with a line for the reviewer under each.

The constraint is that the record has to be usable: photographs carry location information, or the place cannot be found at review; anything scheduled writes down which machine, which shift, how long it takes and who it is stuck with, not just "to be repaired".

The verification step can be fixed: at the same point each week the reviewer signs; anything that cannot be signed goes on an overdue list and is escalated by the shift lead, rather than moved to the next cell and considered done. Shutdown, isolation and approval requirements are not skipped because a signature is missing; items needing qualification or an outside contractor go through the process before being closed.

### The gas hose and the power strip at the parents' flat

(Fictional scene.) Back at the parents' flat for the weekend, both notice the hose by the hob has hardened on the surface and the power strip is carrying a rice cooker and a kettle. They can describe what they noticed and check any maintenance records from a safe place. Either person can gather the same information for a qualified technician.

If a gas leak is suspected, leave the property and contact the local emergency service from a safe distance. The same guidance applies to either person.

Keep the counterexamples: someone leaning to the ESTP side will also press "how many years has this hose been on"; someone leaning to the ISFJ side, smelling gas, will also leave first and not go looking for the records. Agree a checkpoint — once the maintenance is done, ask the parents to repeat what to do first if they smell gas, and which number to call.

### The supervisor wants all eleven closed today

(Fictional scene.) The requirement comes down, and neither usually argues with it directly, but the way of explaining may differ. One more often states which items are risks that must be controlled today and why the rest need a window and parts; the other more often regroups by "can it be done today", reporting separately what needs a shutdown, parts or a contractor. Either may switch to the other wording, depending on whether the supervisor wants a risk conclusion or an executable schedule.

The condition for switching is clear: if the supervisor wants numbers, state the basis first — how many can be controlled today, how many need a window, how overdue items are escalated; if someone on site is already injured, start the emergency response, call for help and prevent secondary harm, then rectify under the process, without treating "closing the item" as a substitute for the emergency.

The inspection example has to keep three kinds of action apart: temporary risk control (isolate, warn, take out of service), authorised repair (implemented once qualification, approval, power isolation and isolation conditions are in place), and review closure (signature and verification of effect). Overdue items are escalated; shutdown, isolation and approval requirements are not skipped because a signature is missing or time is short.
compare_blocks.title: Illustrative scenarios

compare_blocks.body:
Reading someone leaning to the ESTP side as "does not like records" is a common bias. An ESTP can keep a detailed inspection record. Job duties and training shape how it is made. Nor does it follow that they will not talk to people and coordinate temporarily when the process does not cover a case, instead of waiting for the paperwork.

Reading someone leaning to the ISFJ side as "only follows the book" is equally wrong. Following the book is often because the book carries someone else's lesson; facing something the book does not cover, they will judge for themselves and carry it for a colleague. Such a person may also coordinate proactively where the process is missing, instead of leaving the problem on the sheet.

The third misread is gender and post. Carefulness and thoughtfulness are not the property of a type or a gender; nor does it follow that one type is better suited to safety management — that turns a preference into a rank of ability. Both can keep detailed records, and both can coordinate when the process does not cover a case; fitness for a post is judged by qualification, training and experience, not four letters.

body: Reading someone leaning to the ESTP side as "does not like records" is a common bias. An ESTP can keep a detailed inspection record. Job duties and training shape how it is made. Nor does it follow that they will not talk to people and coordinate temporarily when the process does not cover a case, instead of waiting for the paperwork.

Reading someone leaning to the ISFJ side as "only follows the book" is equally wrong. Following the book is often because the book carries someone else's lesson; facing something the book does not cover, they will judge for themselves and carry it for a colleague. Such a person may also coordinate proactively where the process is missing, instead of leaving the problem on the sheet.

The third misread is gender and post. Carefulness and thoughtfulness are not the property of a type or a gender; nor does it follow that one type is better suited to safety management — that turns a preference into a rank of ability. Both can keep detailed records, and both can coordinate when the process does not cover a case; fitness for a post is judged by qualification, training and experience, not four letters.

faq_blocks.answer:
Not assigned by type; divide by authority, experience and shift duty, and have the person on the floor and the reviewer design it together, half each.

The sheet has to hold location, owner, deadline, review date and the decision criterion — what must stop today, what can wait for a window. faq_blocks.answer:
More often differences in habit and boundaries: one feels the other "writes everything down", the other feels the first "never puts things back". That relates to type only indirectly, and also to upbringing, schedule and who moved in first.

A workable agreement lists shared items on a short sheet, and whoever takes something ticks it off; things needing a reminder go in the same place, which is less tiring than persuading each other. Either type can be the one keeping accounts, and either can forget to put something back; treating the friction as a difference in habit is easier to resolve than treating it as a character defect.

sections.title: Quick answer

body: Two people in the same workshop rarely talk in generalities: one watches where an accident could happen, the other remembers who promised what. Part of that resemblance comes from the shared S — both talk in specific locations, specific people and specific dates, and neither stays at the level of slogans. But S only says sourcing prefers facts and experience; it does not say who is more careful, and does not say who is more practical.

The difference sits on three preferences. ESTP more often takes the facts on the floor in front of them (S), with attention and energy turned outward (E); ISFJ more often takes past experience and agreements already confirmed (S), with attention and energy turned inward (I). In judging, ESTP more often relies on criteria that can be applied consistently (T), and ISFJ more often counts people and values in (F). In outer work, ISFJ more often forms an arrangement and a conclusion (J), and ESTP more often keeps options (P).

The three are read separately. They do not combine into a scale of "who is more dependable", and cannot be replaced by "which step came first": registering before handling, and handling before registering, both occur in either person.
### Eleven findings: what each more often sorts by

With eleven items on the table, either may sort by urgency and either by closure. Which kind of basis is cited more often is a description of preference; the actual sequence is also constrained by risk level, qualifications and approval, shift duty, spare-part arrival and shutdown windows.
In this fictional inspection, immediate hazards and recurring problems both need attention. The site procedure determines what needs immediate action, regardless of who notices it.
Once required safety controls are in place, both can check which follow-up actions need an owner, a maintenance window or verification that the issue was resolved.

The two bases are usually mixed on one sheet: contain what has to be isolated immediately, then, with risk controlled, register owners, deadlines and review dates. That combination has nothing to do with type; it is ordinary safety management.

A fictional monthly inspection shows where the difference lies. After eleven findings, one colleague makes sure the findings reach the authorised team. The other confirms which follow-up actions have an owner and a review date, and flags three findings that also appeared last year. Either person could do both. At the month-end review, what tends not to be closed is not the most dangerous items but the ones needing a shutdown window — which has nothing to do with sorting preference and everything to do with maintenance windows, spare parts and approval progress.

Three things evidence the quality of rectification: whether the review record carries a signature, whether the same hazard recurs, and whether window-dependent items were scheduled into the maintenance plan. Those three check rectification quality only and cannot be turned around to infer a type; nor does the speed of the walk or the number of notices issued count.

Keep the counterexamples: asked for a closure rate, someone leaning to the ESTP side may build the sheet themselves and chase review dates; seeing pallets blocking a fire route, someone leaning to the ISFJ side may call people to clear it first and register afterwards. Role, duty, experience and deadline all rewrite the approach.
### Why Ti and Fe are shared but swapped
In the common four-function notation used here, ESTP is Se–Ti–Fe–Ni and ISFJ is Si–Fe–Ti–Ne. The shared Ti and Fe swap: ESTP has Ti second and Fe third, ISFJ has Fe second and Ti third.

The perceiving side changes entirely, direction included: ESTP uses Se to catch the scene and keeps Ni last; ISFJ draws on Si for past experience and keeps Ne last. A function position is an emphasis in the model, not the first and second step of an action, and it does not show who unpicks the causal chain first or who attends to people first.

Whether the third process (Fe for ESTP, Ti for ISFJ) carries an attitude label is not consistent across tables: some give an explicit attitude, some only the function name. This page takes the common version and states the arrangement; the disagreement does not change the first two positions and does not explain why a particular inspection did one item first. Both base descriptions are the [ESTP profile](/en/personality/estp) and the [ISFJ profile](/en/personality/isfj).

body: The premise is aligned conditions: the same monthly inspection, the same eleven findings, the same shutdown window and review deadline, the same approval authority. If one owns the review and the other only handles the shift, or one holds shutdown approval and the other does not, role will cover both columns.

Each row states the basis each may attend to and notes which axis it illustrates. Both types can use both approaches; the table describes only which is taken first more often, and is not a typing rule.

| The same scene (one inspection, the same eleven items, the same authority and deadline) | ESTP: the basis more likely attended to | ISFJ: the basis more likely attended to | What this row illustrates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Both organise follow-up for the same findings after applying mandatory safety controls | Apply the same follow-up criteria to the remaining findings | Weigh how each follow-up option affects the people relying on the area | Basis for judgement, leaning T/F |
| Half a metre of walkway taken by pallets: what to notice now | Whether people can still pass, and whether a route must be cleared first | Who normally owns this area, and how it will not be blocked again | Present access conditions and long-term upkeep; both need checking |
| Items that need a shutdown to fix | Keep feasible maintenance slots open while the same window and parts availability are confirmed | Agree on a provisional slot and owner within the same maintenance constraints | Outward stance, leaning J/P |
| Both use the same verified inspection results to explain what remains open | Use the same completion criteria to decide which unresolved details to explain | Weigh which unresolved details matter most to the people who depend on the follow-up | Basis for judgement, leaning T/F |
| How to fix the review time and the owner | May keep feasible dates and owners open until availability is confirmed | May agree on a provisional review date and owner under the same constraints | Outward stance, leaning J/P |
| After the same inspection, with identical records in hand | Exchange observations with the partner and clarify in conversation what still worries them | Take time alone with the same record, then bring questions back to the partner | E/I: clarifying through interaction or internal sorting; both follow the safety and review process |

The differences in the table are not a scale of ability. Anyone who has managed safety for years, of either type, is more likely to isolate the risk under procedure first; someone taking on an inspection for the first time may only tick the list item by item. The same person also changes approach with shift duty, information and deadline, so these rows cannot be used to classify.

body: Scope note: what follows is a fictional inspection and a household-maintenance scene, covering communication, the organisation of information and negotiation over the division of work only, not handling procedure, qualification judgement or medical first aid. For a smell of gas or an injury, leave the hazardous area first, call for help, and act on local emergency and professional guidance; the type discussion does not enter those judgements.

Working together, the two easily get stuck when one has already started work and the other is still checking the sheet. That is rarely about who is right, but about which kind of information each handles first — or simply about who was closer to the scene.
### After the inspection, who watches the shutdown window

(Fictional scene.) The division follows authority, experience and shift duty, not type. Handling and tracking are complementary tasks: the person on the floor knows what can be controlled on the spot and what it needs; the review owner knows the window, the spare parts and the approval progress. A workable move is for both to design one three-cell card — today, this week, needs a window — with a line for the reviewer under each.

The constraint is that the record has to be usable: photographs carry location information, or the place cannot be found at review; anything scheduled writes down which machine, which shift, how long it takes and who it is stuck with, not just "to be repaired".

The verification step can be fixed: at the same point each week the reviewer signs; anything that cannot be signed goes on an overdue list and is escalated by the shift lead, rather than moved to the next cell and considered done. Shutdown, isolation and approval requirements are not skipped because a signature is missing; items needing qualification or an outside contractor go through the process before being closed.
### The gas hose and the power strip at the parents' flat

(Fictional scene.) Back at the parents' flat for the weekend, both notice the hose by the hob has hardened on the surface and the power strip is carrying a rice cooker and a kettle. They can describe what they noticed and check any maintenance records from a safe place. Either person can gather the same information for a qualified technician.
If a gas leak is suspected, leave the property and contact the local emergency service from a safe distance. The same guidance applies to either person.

Keep the counterexamples: someone leaning to the ESTP side will also press "how many years has this hose been on"; someone leaning to the ISFJ side, smelling gas, will also leave first and not go looking for the records. Agree a checkpoint — once the maintenance is done, ask the parents to repeat what to do first if they smell gas, and which number to call.
### The supervisor wants all eleven closed today

(Fictional scene.) The requirement comes down, and neither usually argues with it directly, but the way of explaining may differ. One more often states which items are risks that must be controlled today and why the rest need a window and parts; the other more often regroups by "can it be done today", reporting separately what needs a shutdown, parts or a contractor. Either may switch to the other wording, depending on whether the supervisor wants a risk conclusion or an executable schedule.

The condition for switching is clear: if the supervisor wants numbers, state the basis first — how many can be controlled today, how many need a window, how overdue items are escalated; if someone on site is already injured, start the emergency response, call for help and prevent secondary harm, then rectify under the process, without treating "closing the item" as a substitute for the emergency.

The inspection example has to keep three kinds of action apart: temporary risk control (isolate, warn, take out of service), authorised repair (implemented once qualification, approval, power isolation and isolation conditions are in place), and review closure (signature and verification of effect). Overdue items are escalated; shutdown, isolation and approval requirements are not skipped because a signature is missing or time is short.

comparison_public_projection_v1.summary:
ESTP and ISFJ share only S, and differ on E/I, T/F and J/P. The shared S means information more often comes from observable facts and past experience, so either person may pay close attention to what was observed and what happened before.

- E/I: the ESTP side, E, turns attention and energy more often to the floor and the people there; the ISFJ side, I, turns more often to their own judgement and accumulated experience. This describes direction, not social skill and not how much someone talks.
- T/F: the ESTP side, T, more often judges by impersonal criteria that can be applied consistently; the ISFJ side, F, more often puts people and values into the judgement.
- J/P: the ISFJ side, J, more often forms an arrangement and a conclusion outward; the ESTP side, P, more often keeps options and adjusts as new information arrives.

In the common four-function notation used here, ESTP is Se–Ti–Fe–Ni and ISFJ is Si–Fe–Ti–Ne. Both stacks contain Ti and Fe, but ESTP puts Ti second and Fe third, and ISFJ the reverse; the attitude of the third process is labelled differently elsewhere, and this writing is a convention adopted here, not the Foundation's only version.

These preferences describe emphasis inside the model. They do not predict the order of actions, or who spots a hazard first, or whether two people work well together. On the same rectification list, either may control the risk before registering it, and either may coordinate resources once the risk is contained; the order depends more on risk level, authority, duty, experience and process.

sections.title: Quick answer

sections.body_md:
Two people in the same workshop rarely talk in generalities: one watches where an accident could happen, the other remembers who promised what. Part of that resemblance comes from the shared S — both talk in specific locations, specific people and specific dates, and neither stays at the level of slogans. But S only says sourcing prefers facts and experience; it does not say who is more careful, and does not say who is more practical.

The difference sits on three preferences. ESTP more often takes the facts on the floor in front of them (S), with attention and energy turned outward (E); ISFJ more often takes past experience and agreements already confirmed (S), with attention and energy turned inward (I). In judging, ESTP more often relies on criteria that can be applied consistently (T), and ISFJ more often counts people and values in (F). In outer work, ISFJ more often forms an arrangement and a conclusion (J), and ESTP more often keeps options (P).

The three are read separately. They do not combine into a scale of "who is more dependable", and cannot be replaced by "which step came first": registering before handling, and handling before registering, both occur in either person.

### Eleven findings: what each more often sorts by

With eleven items on the table, either may sort by urgency and either by closure. Which kind of basis is cited more often is a description of preference; the actual sequence is also constrained by risk level, qualifications and approval, shift duty, spare-part arrival and shutdown windows.

In this fictional inspection, immediate hazards and recurring problems both need attention. The site procedure determines what needs immediate action, regardless of who notices it.

Once required safety controls are in place, both can check which follow-up actions need an owner, a maintenance window or verification that the issue was resolved.

The two bases are usually mixed on one sheet: contain what has to be isolated immediately, then, with risk controlled, register owners, deadlines and review dates. That combination has nothing to do with type; it is ordinary safety management.

A fictional monthly inspection shows where the difference lies. After eleven findings, one colleague makes sure the findings reach the authorised team. The other confirms which follow-up actions have an owner and a review date, and flags three findings that also appeared last year. Either person could do both. At the month-end review, what tends not to be closed is not the most dangerous items but the ones needing a shutdown window — which has nothing to do with sorting preference and everything to do with maintenance windows, spare parts and approval progress.

Three things evidence the quality of rectification: whether the review record carries a signature, whether the same hazard recurs, and whether window-dependent items were scheduled into the maintenance plan. Those three check rectification quality only and cannot be turned around to infer a type; nor does the speed of the walk or the number of notices issued count.

Keep the counterexamples: asked for a closure rate, someone leaning to the ESTP side may build the sheet themselves and chase review dates; seeing pallets blocking a fire route, someone leaning to the ISFJ side may call people to clear it first and register afterwards. Role, duty, experience and deadline all rewrite the approach.

### Why Ti and Fe are shared but swapped

In the common four-function notation used here, ESTP is Se–Ti–Fe–Ni and ISFJ is Si–Fe–Ti–Ne. The shared Ti and Fe swap: ESTP has Ti second and Fe third, ISFJ has Fe second and Ti third.

The perceiving side changes entirely, direction included: ESTP uses Se to catch the scene and keeps Ni last; ISFJ draws on Si for past experience and keeps Ne last. A function position is an emphasis in the model, not the first and second step of an action, and it does not show who unpicks the causal chain first or who attends to people first.

Whether the third process (Fe for ESTP, Ti for ISFJ) carries an attitude label is not consistent across tables: some give an explicit attitude, some only the function name. This page takes the common version and states the arrangement; the disagreement does not change the first two positions and does not explain why a particular inspection did one item first. Both base descriptions are the [ESTP profile](/en/personality/estp) and the [ISFJ profile](/en/personality/isfj).

sections.body_md:
The premise is aligned conditions: the same monthly inspection, the same eleven findings, the same shutdown window and review deadline, the same approval authority. If one owns the review and the other only handles the shift, or one holds shutdown approval and the other does not, role will cover both columns.

Each row states the basis each may attend to and notes which axis it illustrates. Both types can use both approaches; the table describes only which is taken first more often, and is not a typing rule.

| The same scene (one inspection, the same eleven items, the same authority and deadline) | ESTP: the basis more likely attended to | ISFJ: the basis more likely attended to | What this row illustrates |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Both organise follow-up for the same findings after applying mandatory safety controls | Apply the same follow-up criteria to the remaining findings | Weigh how each follow-up option affects the people relying on the area | Basis for judgement, leaning T/F |
| Half a metre of walkway taken by pallets: what to notice now | Whether people can still pass, and whether a route must be cleared first | Who normally owns this area, and how it will not be blocked again | Present access conditions and long-term upkeep; both need checking |
| Items that need a shutdown to fix | Keep feasible maintenance slots open while the same window and parts availability are confirmed | Agree on a provisional slot and owner within the same maintenance constraints | Outward stance, leaning J/P |
| Both use the same verified inspection results to explain what remains open | Use the same completion criteria to decide which unresolved details to explain | Weigh which unresolved details matter most to the people who depend on the follow-up | Basis for judgement, leaning T/F |
| How to fix the review time and the owner | May keep feasible dates and owners open until availability is confirmed | May agree on a provisional review date and owner under the same constraints | Outward stance, leaning J/P |
| After the same inspection, with identical records in hand | Exchange observations with the partner and clarify in conversation what still worries them | Take time alone with the same record, then bring questions back to the partner | E/I: clarifying through interaction or internal sorting; both follow the safety and review process |

The differences in the table are not a scale of ability. Anyone who has managed safety for years, of either type, is more likely to isolate the risk under procedure first; someone taking on an inspection for the first time may only tick the list item by item. The same person also changes approach with shift duty, information and deadline, so these rows cannot be used to classify.
sections.title: ESTP and ISFJ in one minute

sections.body_md:
Scope note: what follows is a fictional inspection and a household-maintenance scene, covering communication, the organisation of information and negotiation over the division of work only, not handling procedure, qualification judgement or medical first aid. For a smell of gas or an injury, leave the hazardous area first, call for help, and act on local emergency and professional guidance; the type discussion does not enter those judgements.

Working together, the two easily get stuck when one has already started work and the other is still checking the sheet. That is rarely about who is right, but about which kind of information each handles first — or simply about who was closer to the scene.

### After the inspection, who watches the shutdown window

(Fictional scene.) The division follows authority, experience and shift duty, not type. Handling and tracking are complementary tasks: the person on the floor knows what can be controlled on the spot and what it needs; the review owner knows the window, the spare parts and the approval progress. A workable move is for both to design one three-cell card — today, this week, needs a window — with a line for the reviewer under each.

The constraint is that the record has to be usable: photographs carry location information, or the place cannot be found at review; anything scheduled writes down which machine, which shift, how long it takes and who it is stuck with, not just "to be repaired".

The verification step can be fixed: at the same point each week the reviewer signs; anything that cannot be signed goes on an overdue list and is escalated by the shift lead, rather than moved to the next cell and considered done. Shutdown, isolation and approval requirements are not skipped because a signature is missing; items needing qualification or an outside contractor go through the process before being closed.

### The gas hose and the power strip at the parents' flat

(Fictional scene.) Back at the parents' flat for the weekend, both notice the hose by the hob has hardened on the surface and the power strip is carrying a rice cooker and a kettle. They can describe what they noticed and check any maintenance records from a safe place. Either person can gather the same information for a qualified technician.

If a gas leak is suspected, leave the property and contact the local emergency service from a safe distance. The same guidance applies to either person.

Keep the counterexamples: someone leaning to the ESTP side will also press "how many years has this hose been on"; someone leaning to the ISFJ side, smelling gas, will also leave first and not go looking for the records. Agree a checkpoint — once the maintenance is done, ask the parents to repeat what to do first if they smell gas, and which number to call.

### The supervisor wants all eleven closed today

(Fictional scene.) The requirement comes down, and neither usually argues with it directly, but the way of explaining may differ. One more often states which items are risks that must be controlled today and why the rest need a window and parts; the other more often regroups by "can it be done today", reporting separately what needs a shutdown, parts or a contractor. Either may switch to the other wording, depending on whether the supervisor wants a risk conclusion or an executable schedule.

The condition for switching is clear: if the supervisor wants numbers, state the basis first — how many can be controlled today, how many need a window, how overdue items are escalated; if someone on site is already injured, start the emergency response, call for help and prevent secondary harm, then rectify under the process, without treating "closing the item" as a substitute for the emergency.

The inspection example has to keep three kinds of action apart: temporary risk control (isolate, warn, take out of service), authorised repair (implemented once qualification, approval, power isolation and isolation conditions are in place), and review closure (signature and verification of effect). Overdue items are escalated; shutdown, isolation and approval requirements are not skipped because a signature is missing or time is short.
sections.title: ESTP and ISFJ at work and in relationships

sections.body_md:
Reading someone leaning to the ESTP side as "does not like records" is a common bias. An ESTP can keep a detailed inspection record. Job duties and training shape how it is made. Nor does it follow that they will not talk to people and coordinate temporarily when the process does not cover a case, instead of waiting for the paperwork.

Reading someone leaning to the ISFJ side as "only follows the book" is equally wrong. Following the book is often because the book carries someone else's lesson; facing something the book does not cover, they will judge for themselves and carry it for a colleague. Such a person may also coordinate proactively where the process is missing, instead of leaving the problem on the sheet.

The third misread is gender and post. Carefulness and thoughtfulness are not the property of a type or a gender; nor does it follow that one type is better suited to safety management — that turns a preference into a rank of ability. Both can keep detailed records, and both can coordinate when the process does not cover a case; fitness for a post is judged by qualification, training and experience, not four letters.
sections.title: ESTP and ISFJ: avoiding misreads

sections.body_md:
When two results differ, check the item bank, language version, scoring convention and the scene you answered from, rather than reasoning backwards into "I must have acted first". The review owner keeps accounts without noticing, and the person handling keeps watching the floor without noticing; those differences come from duty, and may also run in the same direction as preference — the two have to be separated.

Put the practice in non-urgent situations with similar roles: take a few recent comparable settings — the same kind of inspection, the same rectification sheet, the same household job — and write three lines for each: what options were available, what constrained you (authority, deadline, parts, approval), and which basis decided the trade-off. If "has this risk reached the point of needing control now" or "who is affected and who promised what" keeps appearing, that is worth discussing as your judging habit.

These notes are for reflection, not a typing rule: no assigning a type from frequency, sequence or rectification results, and the two bases alternating is common. If a basis appears only in a particular post, suspect the duty before discussing preference.
sections.title: ESTP and ISFJ: how to keep observing

items.answer:
No missing item can be asserted by type, but two blind spots are common: someone sorting by urgency easily misses "who reviews it afterwards" — the situation is controlled and nobody signs the closure; someone sorting by closure easily misses the item that is dangerous today, because it may not be in the order already set.

Both have symmetric fixes: the first adds a reviewer cell, the second adds a "must be done today" criterion. What actually decides whether something is missed is shift duty, experience, information and deadline, not four letters; and the fix does not need dividing — whoever spots the gap fills it.
items.question: On a safety inspection, what does each tend to miss?

items.answer:
In the common four-function notation used here, the two swap Ti and Fe: ESTP is Se–Ti–Fe–Ni and ISFJ is Si–Fe–Ti–Ne. That is a description of preference in the model; it does not say who analyses first or who considers people first, and cannot explain why one inspection did a particular item first.

Also, whether the third process (Fe for ESTP, Ti for ISFJ) carries an attitude label is not consistent across sources, some giving only the function name. "Floor type" and "ledger type" are shorthand for description; with different duties and deadlines, either side can move to the other; and positions do not predict a field of expertise, the effect of collaboration or attraction.
items.question: Both have Ti and Fe — why does one look like the floor type and the other like the ledger type?

items.answer:
Yes, either may handle it on the spot and either may register first. Whether to act immediately depends on the risk level, your authority, the isolation conditions and the shift duty, and is governed by the same safety requirements for either type.

The basis is not "did they act" but which reason was cited at the time: whether the risk has reached the point of needing control now, whether this item sits within your authority, and who reviews it afterwards. Someone leaning to the ISFJ side will also call people to clear a blocked walkway and register afterwards; someone leaning to the ESTP side, asked for a closure rate, will also complete the sheet first.
items.question: Will ISFJ also start rectifying on the spot, and ESTP register first?

items.answer:
Not assigned by type; divide by authority, experience and shift duty, and have the person on the floor and the reviewer design it together, half each.

The sheet has to hold location, owner, deadline, review date and the decision criterion — what must stop today, what can wait for a window. The on-site criterion is written by whoever knows the equipment and the risk; tracking and closure are maintained by whoever owns the review. After designing it, each uses it once and then revises; whoever finds it awkward says so on the spot, and either side may raise the line the other missed.
items.question: Who should design the inspection sheet?

items.answer:
More often differences in habit and boundaries: one feels the other "writes everything down", the other feels the first "never puts things back". That relates to type only indirectly, and also to upbringing, schedule and who moved in first.

A workable agreement lists shared items on a short sheet, and whoever takes something ticks it off; things needing a reminder go in the same place, which is less tiring than persuading each other. Either type can be the one keeping accounts, and either can forget to put something back; treating the friction as a difference in habit is easier to resolve than treating it as a character defect.
items.question: Sharing a dormitory, what do they most often resent in each other?

items.answer:
Not one item. Look first at the answering context: were you referring to a process requirement at work or to a habit at home, and were you being pushed by a duty, a recent task or a social expectation.

If the item bank reports dimension scores, look at whether E/I, T/F or J/P sits nearer the boundary. Sitting near a boundary only means that label is sensitive to changes in your answers, not that two complete types both hold; without dimension scores or scoring notes, do not infer a boundary, and no retest interval is prescribed. Another version or a retest months later is for reference only.

Framework sources: the preference definitions follow the [official Myers-Briggs facts page](https://www.myersbriggs.com/en-us/support/mbti-facts); the type dynamics framework follows the [Foundation's account of type dynamics processes](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-processes/) and the [type dynamics overview](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-overview/).

Four-position convention: Se–Ti–Fe–Ni for ESTP and Si–Fe–Ti–Ne for ISFJ use the common arrangement; the full four positions, especially the attitude of the third process, is the labelling convention of this page. Sources handle it differently, and this writing is not presented as the Foundation's only version; citing the basis is enough.

Editorial fiction: the eleven findings, the shutdown-window coordination, the parents' hose and power strip, and the instruction to close everything today are editorial fictions, written to illustrate communication and planning, corresponding to no real organisation or person, and constituting no safety procedure or medical advice.

Scope limits: this page discusses emphasis in preference, does not rate ability, and is not for hiring, job fit or predicting relationships. Risks involving gas, electricity or work at height follow local regulation, site procedure and professional guidance; where someone is injured, seek help first and follow first-aid guidance. Assessment results are a reference for self-understanding only. The FermatMind assessment uses its own item bank and scoring; the scope is set out in the [scoring and evidence note](/en/tests/mbti-personality-test-16-personality-types#method-and-evidence).
